validated.title: Auth token (JWT) stored in plaintext SharedPreferences
validated.description: AuthManager writes the session JWT to SharedPreferences via a plain putString() call, with no platform Keystore/EncryptedSharedPreferences wrapping. The value is stored in cleartext XML under the app's data directory.
validated.impact: Any attacker with physical/adb access to the device (or a backup extracted via allowBackup=true) can read the SharedPreferences XML file and obtain a live session token, enabling account takeover without the user's password.

evidence.user_input_source: n/a — value is the session token issued at login, not user input
evidence.data_flow: login response JWT -> AuthManager.saveSession() -> SharedPreferences (plaintext) -> read back on every API call via AuthManager.getToken()
evidence.missing_check: Use EncryptedSharedPreferences (Jetpack Security) or store only a reference to a key held in Android Keystore, not the raw JWT.
evidence.notes: Compounded by AndroidManifest.xml android:allowBackup="true" with no fullBackupContent exclusion, so `adb backup` can extract this file without root.

validated.validation_notes: Re-traced saveSession()/getToken() call sites; confirmed no EncryptedSharedPreferences or Keystore usage anywhere in the auth package, and confirmed allowBackup=true in the release manifest.
validated.remediation: Migrate to EncryptedSharedPreferences or store the token only in memory + Android Keystore-backed encryption. Set android:allowBackup="false" or add fullBackupContent rules excluding the auth prefs file. Add a short token lifetime + refresh flow to limit exposure window.

validated.title: Unguarded exported DeepLinkActivity allows triggering password reset
validated.description: DeepLinkActivity is exported (implicitly, via an intent-filter for the acmebank:// scheme) with no permission or signature guard, and directly consumes the `token` query parameter from the incoming Intent to drive the password-reset flow, with no validation that the Intent originated from the app's own reset-password email link.
validated.impact: A malicious app on the same device can send an Intent to acmebank://reset-password?token=<attacker-controlled> and drive the victim's app into a reset flow using an attacker-supplied token, potentially completing an account takeover if combined with a way to obtain a valid reset token (e.g. a separate token-prediction or leakage issue).

evidence.user_input_source: getIntent().getData() (deep link Uri, can originate from any app)
evidence.missing_check: Verify the Intent's calling package (getCallingPackage()) or require App Links / Digital Asset Links verification instead of a plain custom scheme, and re-validate the token server-side before acting on it.
evidence.notes: AndroidManifest.xml declares the intent-filter with no android:permission attribute.

validated.validation_notes: Confirmed the intent-filter is registered with no permission attribute in AndroidManifest.xml, and confirmed onCreate() performs no calling-package or Digital Asset Links check before acting on the token.
validated.remediation: Migrate from a custom URL scheme to Android App Links with Digital Asset Links (assetlinks.json) verification, which restricts which apps can trigger the link. Re-validate the reset token server-side (single-use, short-lived) regardless of client-side checks.

rejected.reason: Candidate flagged network_security_config.xml cleartextTrafficPermitted="true" for legacy-metrics.acmebank.example as Critical, but re-tracing confirmed that domain only ever receives anonymous, non-sensitive analytics counters (no auth tokens, no PII) — downgraded scope makes this Low, not Critical; kept as informational in the report, not a standalone finding.

merged.reason: AccountDao.java's plaintext SQLite cache of account_number/balance shares the same root cause (no EncryptedSharedPreferences/Keystore usage in local persistence) as the auth-token finding — merged into one Insecure Data Storage finding covering both storage locations.
